text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein arrives in Holland at the start of a European tour which includes France and Britain.
- King Hussein reviews prevailing conditions in the region and peace developments with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak by telephone.
- An agreement by 10 opposition parties to contest the elections on joint platform is prompted by the present political climate, opposition sources say.
- Jordan reschedules $400 million debt owed to the Paris Club of official creditors.
- Crown Prince Hassan to start a tour on Thursday to include the United States, Turkey and European countries.
- A new draft law to regulate professional unions proposes cancelling the compulsory membership clause and penalising unions that engage in politics.
- The National Contitutional Party which came into being from a merger of nine parties to be formally launched on Wednesday.
- King's and Crown prince's foreign tours aim at containing regional crises and attracting support and investments and activating Middle East peace.
- Interior Minister starts probe into party complaince with law.
- Crown prince calls upon donors to continue supporting U.N. body responsible for Palestinian refugees.
